_comment: What tools/harness.py exports, boots and checks, and what each capture must prove.
Every project here is exported through the REAL pipeline and the exported game
is what gets booted, because that is the render path which had no capture
coverage at all. Testing the project folder instead would measure a path no
frames: which frame ordinals to photograph. Two, far apart, because one picture
cannot tell a still scene from a stopped one. The first is late enough that boot
defaults are no longer on screen.
claims.draws: the frame is not one flat colour.
claims.animates.min_changed_pct: how much of the frame must move between the
first and last capture. This is the claim that catches a feature which renders
a perfectly valid frame and was never switched on.
animates starts ON for every project. A project that legitimately does not move
gets it turned OFF here WITH A REASON on the entry, never silently: a demo that
is meant to be still and a demo whose animation broke look identical from the
outside, and the difference has to be written down by a person who checked.

PaletteCycling is why this exists. On 2026-09-16 its exported build was byte-identical across seven captures spanning 6.5 seconds while authoring two palettes cycling at 6 entries/sec. Root cause: the player calls World::Update(0.0f), so nothing ever deposited a real dt in the palette clock. Fixed in Player/src/main.cpp; this project now moves 8.65%.

FOUR capture points, not two. Two was the first design and it was not sound: ShadowCheck reported 60.29% moved and then 0.00% on two identical runs of the same binary. Captures are taken by frame ORDINAL while scenes move on a clock, so two samples can land on the same phase of a loop, or both land after a physics scene has come to rest. animates now passes if ANY pair differs.

"ci": true marks the projects the CI gate runs (--ci). Three, not 26, because CI renders on lavapipe in software and a gate that takes an hour is a gate nobody waits for. Each one is there for a stated reason on its entry; the full sweep stays a thing a person runs locally.

projects.name: BiscuitBird
projects._determinism: f0500 is NOT reproducible: it takes one value inside a full sweep and another captured alone, both reproducibly. 848 px in a 75x27 box on the TAIL of the on-screen string '...of centre to steer' -- UI text, not geometry. Measured 2026-09-21; run tools/harness.py --repeat before trusting an A/B here.

projects.name: FixedTimestep
projects._web_frames_why: A browser cannot be photographed at simulation frame 30: the preloader, the Click-to-Play gate and the clicking needed to get through them take real time, and the earliest reachable frame here was measured at about 120. The demo replays itself every 4 seconds (240 frames), so these four land at cycle phases 150, 200, 20 and 90 -- ball settled, still settled, just reset, mid-fall. Asking for the desktop frames instead returned four photographs of the same settled pile, which is what made this project read as FROZEN on web.

projects.name: FluidSim
projects._determinism: f0500 is NOT reproducible across three runs in one context -- genuinely nondeterministic, 8811 px over a 388x339 region of the simulation. Measured 2026-09-21; an A/B against this frame needs repeats on both sides.

projects.name: HandIK
projects.animates_off_because: SETTLED 2026-09-16, having been left failing on purpose until somebody looked. The animator component that made it suspicious is serialized as {"speed": 1.0} and nothing else -- no clip, no state machine, so there is nothing to play. The hand IK engages on proximity (engageDistance 0.45) and the first-person player has to walk to a surface to trigger it, which the harness never does. Still under no input, legitimately. Worth noting separately that a demo of hand IK shows none of it to somebody who just launches it.

projects.name: PaletteCycling
projects.ci_because: REGRESSION GUARD for 424a4551: palette cycling had never run in an exported game and this project is the only thing that proves it does. It failed `animates` at 0.00% before that fix and passes at 19% after.

projects.name: Potions

projects.name: ReflectionProbes
projects.animates_off_because: Two static probe-placement scenes, no script and no animator. Checked 2026-09-16.

projects.name: RoomAcoustics
projects.animates_off_because: An AUDIO demo. Its one script plays a clap on input and moves nothing; a still picture is the correct result. Worth its own claim on sound one day, not on pixels. Checked 2026-09-16.
projects.hears_because: Eleven rooms whose entire point is that they sound different. Judged on pixels it is a still photograph and always will be, so the pixel claims can never say whether the demo works. This one goes through AudioEngine, which is where the reverb bus being compiled out and the listener being frozen at the origin both hid from twelve green DSP suites.

projects.name: ShadowCheck
projects.animates_off_because: A third-person controller and nothing else that moves: no script, no animator. The player stands where it lands and the camera holds. Its earlier "91% moved" was the boot-time drop caught mid-fall on a loaded machine, which is what led to the fixed-timestep capture. Checked 2026-09-16.

projects.name: SpritePivot
projects.animates_off_because: Three sprites at one rotation demonstrating pivot points. Deliberately still. Checked 2026-09-16.

projects.name: Water2D
projects.ci_because: The 2D path: sprites, the batched sprite draw call, and the 2D water overlay. Its `renders` claim caught the sprite batch counting no draws at all (2cd5991b).

projects.name: WaterVolume
projects.ci_because: The 3D path: meshes, a water volume with shore foam and a procedural sky, and something that visibly moves.

projects.name: tmpl-accessibility
projects.animates_off_because: Not asserted for templates. A starting point is not a demo: several ship a static scene on purpose, and the useful question about a template is whether it still BOOTS and DRAWS after a year of engine changes, not whether it entertains you. Turn it on per template if one is meant to move.

projects.name: MaterialModes
projects.note: adr-0008 reference corpus: one cube per material mode, cel shading ON. Captured so a flag-word or permutation change is a pixel diff rather than a judgement.

projects.name: SurfaceBands
projects._why: Every surfaceParam band the cascade can claim, in band order, so a capture diff says WHICH band moved. Verified against a stripped control (python tools/make_coverage_demos.py --control): 100 dither gradient, 200 dither transparency, 300 elemental, 400 surface noise and 500 palette all change the picture. Band 600 lightmapped is deliberately NOT here -- without a baked lightmap it renders identical to a plain material, which is coverage that covers nothing; the Lightmap project has the bake, and that 600 beats 500 for the slot is pinned by TestMaterialDrawState.
projects._animates_why: The palette on the 500 cube cycles at 6 entries/sec, so this scene DOES move and the claim is kept on: it is the only thing here that would notice palette cycling stopping.
projects._editor_why: The surfaceParam cascade now has one definition and three callers. This is the editor-side caller.

projects.name: ArtStyles
projects._why: The four per-entity ArtStyleComponent overrides. All four verified against a stripped control: PrePBR, CelToon, Retro and MaterialExpression each change the picture. NPR, PixelArt and Analog are full-screen styles applied from the camera, so a per-entity cube would prove nothing about them and they are left out rather than included to make the row look complete.
projects._animates_why: OFF: these are static shading overrides and nothing in the scene moves. That is the point -- a diff here means the art-style path changed, not that a clock stopped.
projects._editor_why: The per-entity art-style overrides were missing from two of the three push-constant builders; the editor viewport is the path that HAD them, so it is worth watching from both sides.

projects.name: Splitscreen
projects._why: Two viewports over the same surfaceParam band row. It covers the MAIN PASS in splitscreen mode -- the player sets m_MainPassViewports and RenderSystem::Update renders each viewport itself. It does NOT cover RenderSplitscreen, which is called only from EditorLayer and still has no coverage at all; that was assumed when this project was added and measured false when a diagnostic in RenderSplitscreen logged nothing. The two cameras look from different places on purpose: two halves that matched would pass a draws claim while proving only that one view got copied twice. It earned itself immediately by catching GPU-driven rendering deleting the ground from both halves.
projects._animates_why: The palette on the 500 cube cycles, same as SurfaceBands, so this scene moves.
projects._editor_why: RenderSplitscreen is called ONLY from EditorLayer, so this is the only way that function is exercised at all.

projects.name: LODLadder
projects._why: Identical LOD'd spheres at increasing distance, so one frame shows the whole ladder. LODComponent was made real on 2026-09-21 and had no capture at all, which is a poor state for a feature whose failure mode is silent: a wrong metric does not crash or vanish, it picks the wrong mesh, and the coarsest mesh of a smooth object still looks like the object. sourceMaxExtent is left at 0 on purpose -- that is the legacy case whose metric divided by an unset AABB, went negative, and pinned every such entity to its coarsest level in every exported game.
projects._animates_why: OFF: nothing in the scene moves. A LOD ladder is a still comparison.

projects.name: AnimationLOD
projects._determinism: f0030 differs between two full sweeps (1547 px on the NEAR rig, a pose difference) while three solo runs agree. Whether that is the demo or the engine has not been separated. Measured 2026-09-21.
projects._why: Four identical swaying rigs at increasing distance, each gated by an AnimationLODComponent. The component shipped on 2026-09-21 with unit tests and NO capture, because nothing in the harness had a rigged model in it -- HandIK has the only skeleton in Examples and its animator carries no clip. Unit tests pin the band arithmetic; they cannot tell you the gate is wired to the animator, and a rate gate that is computed and never applied looks exactly like one that works. The control (make_coverage_demos.py --control) is the gate DISABLED, same rigs and same clip, so a byte-identical pair means the feature did nothing.
projects._animates_why: The near rig is in the 0 Hz band, which means unthrottled, so it sways every frame. A still capture here would mean the animator is not ticking at all.

projects.name: WaterFoam
projects._why: Water3DSettings::enableFoam had no capture anywhere, and the reason it needed one is the reason it was broken: the foam block existed in RenderToTarget (the editor viewport) and RenderSplitscreen and NOT in RenderEntity, which is editor play mode and every exported game. Foam appeared while you authored it and vanished from the build, which reads as an art problem rather than a missing branch. Control (make_coverage_demos.py --control) is enableFoam OFF with every other water setting identical, so a byte-identical pair means the flag reached no shader. VertexWave style on purpose -- the foam block is skipped for Refractive water, so a Refractive demo would prove nothing while looking deliberate.
projects._animates_why: Gerstner waves move the surface every frame; a still capture would mean the water mesh is not being regenerated.
projects._web_why: Also carries the web half. The web path set only the water-surface bit for a Water3D plane and none of its authored settings, so foam was absent there too -- and web needs no flag bit, it gates foam on the parameters being non-zero.

projects.name: CustomShader
projects._why: CustomShaderComponent had no capture, which matters more than it looks: the shader graph is an EDITOR tool and the thing it produces is meant to survive into a build. A persisted shader is recompiled at the next FlushPendingChanges in whatever runtime loads the scene, so what a capture answers is not 'does the graph work' but 'does its output reach a game' -- the question this engine keeps getting wrong. Two identical spheres, one wearing the shader and one on the stock material as an in-frame reference: if both look the same, the custom pipeline was never bound, and that is visible in one picture. The shader reads pc.baseColor and lighting.cameraPos on purpose, so the capture also proves the SHARED pipeline layout is intact -- a custom pipeline binding its own descriptors would still draw, just with nonsense in those. Control (make_coverage_demos.py --control) drops the component.
projects._animates_why: OFF: nothing in the scene moves. This is a still comparison between two spheres.

projects.name: MeshRendererFilters
projects._why: MeshRendererComponent is authored by NO project in the corpus -- measured with tools/feature_coverage.py rather than remembered, which is how this gap was found. It matters more than an ordinary hole because all three filters it carries were recently inert: `enabled` did nothing at all, `renderLayerMask` and the camera's cullingMask were never compared, and maxDrawDistance is the kind of guarded test that silently inverts. Each was fixed and nothing since could tell you if one broke again. Four spheres, three of which must be INVISIBLE for three different reasons, so a filter that stops working makes a sphere APPEAR -- a failure that adds something obvious rather than removing something you have to look for. The first sphere is unfiltered on purpose: an empty capture would otherwise be indistinguishable from a project that failed to load. Control (make_coverage_demos.py --control) makes every filter permissive, so all four draw.
projects._animates_why: OFF: nothing in the scene moves. This is a still visibility test.

projects.name: Reflections
projects._why: The implicit scene-wide reflection probe. It is on in every project that has no ReflectionProbeComponent, which is nearly all of them, and NOTHING rendered it under test until 2026-09-23 -- which is how it spent two days painting hard-edged squares across a floor while `draws` and `animates` both passed it. Blocks stacked on one vertical line on purpose: that is the arrangement whose bounds go degenerate, and spread out the bug does not reproduce.

smooth._region: Near floor, below the blocks and their shadows, clear of the horizon ramp. MEASURED either side of the fix: 6.91 of 255 on the engine with the bug, 0.55 with it fixed. The ceiling sits between them with room on both sides. Aimed wider, at a band that included the floor's own edge gradient, both states failed at ~2.0 and the claim proved nothing.

claims._animates_why: OMITTED, which is how this manifest turns the claim off: harness.py skips it when the key is absent. Nothing in this scene moves, on purpose -- the whole point is a still frame whose SHAPE is checked, and `smooth` is the claim that checks it.

projects.name: GaussianSplat
projects._why: The 3D Gaussian splat path: SplatLoader, SplatRenderer and splat.vert/frag had no project at all, so nothing loaded a .ply or drew a gaussian under test. The asset is GENERATED by tools/make_coverage_demos.py rather than a captured scan, so it is regenerable and reviewable as code: three coloured axis bars plus a rotated diagonal one. Axes because a splat cloud is the one asset where 'it rendered something' proves nothing -- a wrong handedness, an undecoded scale or an ignored rotation all still draw a plausible haze. Red is +X, green +Y, blue +Z, the bars are anisotropic so an ignored scale_1/scale_2 shows as blobs, and the diagonal bar is the only part that fails if rot_0 is read as x instead of w.

claims._animates_why: OMITTED: nothing in this scene moves. The 'white streaks' once reported for this demo were never in the frame: the RGB was correct and the capture PNG carried the target's alpha, which blended draws stamped with their own low value (fixed in VulkanPipeline and WriteCapture). That is why a colour claim 'measured MORE colour in the white capture' -- it was reading the true RGB. What this entry proves is that the loader parses, the renderer draws and the pipeline builds. Colour fidelity has no claim yet.
